paper_title: Search for oscillations of fundamental constants using molecular spectroscopy
coupling_convention: dimensionless coupling d_g (scalar coupling to baryonic matter / nuclear masses)
notes: Paper constrains oscillations of fundamental constants (nuclear masses, QCD scale, quark masses) via molecular iodine spectroscopy. Two experiments (A: 10 Hz–100 kHz, B: 100 kHz–100 MHz) probe time-varying nuclear masses through vibrational transitions. The primary exclusion plots (Figs. 3–5) show bounds on combinations of couplings d_g, d_m̂, d_δm, d_ms (to QCD sector) and d_α, d_me (to electromagnetic and electron sectors). The paper's main result is on the coupling vector Q̂_N·d̃ = 0.999 d_gs + 0.092 d_m̂ + 3×10^-4 d_δm + 0.047 d_ms, which is dominated by the gluon coupling d_gs. This is fundamentally a scalar-baryon (or scalar-nucleon) coupling, as it constrains the interaction of a scalar UDM field to nuclear/quark degrees of freedom. The coupling_type ScalarBaryon is chosen because the paper's primary sensitivity is to nuclear mass variations (which depend on the QCD scale and light quark masses), not to a specific nucleon spin coupling. Data extraction is challenging because: (1) the paper presents bounds as functions of frequency f_φ (not mass m_φ directly, though m_φ = f_φ × h/c²), (2) multiple coupling combinations are constrained simultaneously, and (3) the exclusion plots show bounds on linear combinations rather than individual couplings. The data_points array represents approximate bounds across the frequency range 10 Hz–100 MHz (corresponding to m_φ ≈ 4×10^-14 to 4×10^-7 eV) and coupling strengths ranging from ~10^-3 to ~10^-12 (inferred from Figs. 3–5). The galactic halo DM density ρ_DM ≈ 0.3 GeV/cm³ is used in the standard scenario. Extraction confidence is moderate (0.65) because: (1) the coupling type is clear from the physics (scalar-baryon), but (2) the paper does not provide a simple table of (mass, coupling) pairs—bounds are presented as functions of frequency and involve linear combinations of multiple couplings, requiring interpretation.
